Easy.q: What does it mean to 'Parameterize' a Playwright test?
options: To add comments to the test.
To write a single test template and run it multiple times automatically using an array of different data inputs.
To run tests in parallel across multiple machines.
To measure the performance metrics of the test.
Easy.a: To write a single test template and run it multiple times automatically using an array of different data inputs.
Easy.explanation: Parameterization (Data-Driven Testing) eliminates code duplication. If you need to test 10 different search queries, you don't write 10 test blocks; you write 1 test block wrapped in a loop iterating over an array of 10 strings.

Easy.q: While technically valid JavaScript, why is this manual `forEach` loop an anti-pattern for Cross-Browser parameterization in Playwright?

Import the JSON file at the top of your test file, and wrap the `test()` block in a `for...of` loop. Playwright evaluates the file synchronously before execution, recognizing the loop and dynamically registering 50 independent, parallel-capable tests.

Medium.explanation: Data strategy is more important than code. A framework running 500 redundant tests is a waste of money. A framework running 10 perfectly engineered boundary tests is an enterprise asset.

Medium.q: While generating dynamic data *inside* the test works, why does this break Visual Regression Testing (VRT) and Snapshot Testing (`toMatchSnapshot`)?
